scope: Read-only local visual review of assigned title and complete rendered ItemBody previews; no live HTTP/site.

findings.symptom: The source uses a display-math line, but the preview HTML emits it as an inline KaTeX span within the definition paragraph. In the standalone tile the expression starts after “define” and wraps across the next line; the expression tail, including the compact-support condition, is visible before the following prose. The HTML contains the full expression, so no formula omission or clipping is confirmed. The prose after it reaches the screenshot right edge.
findings.suggested_repair: Preserve display-math block layout in the preview HTML so this long definition is visually separated from the prose. No content recovery is needed.

preview_evidence.html_observation: The complete KaTeX MathML and HTML for the formula are present in a katex span after “define”; the element has no katex-display wrapper.
preview_evidence.css_observation: The local custom rule gives main a fixed 1104px width. There is no explicit overflow-x scrolling rule on this content container. The formula tail is visible through normal line wrapping in the screenshot, so horizontal scrolling is not needed to expose it.

findings.excerpt: 4: title: "FALSE: the point values X_p and Y_p determine the bracket value [X,Y]_p"
findings.symptom: Raw ASCII subscript and bracket notation is shown in the title (X_p, Y_p, [X,Y]_p), rather than typeset math.
findings.suggested_repair: Typeset the point and bracket notation in the title using the supported math delimiters.

findings.excerpt: 4: title: "Spin structures exist exactly when w2 vanishes and then form an H1 torsor"
findings.symptom: Characteristic class and cohomology group appear as plain w2 and H1 in the title, without mathematical subscripts/superscripts.
findings.suggested_repair: Typeset the characteristic class and cohomology group in the title with their intended indices.

findings.excerpt: 4: title: The distance from p is smooth on m minus p
findings.symptom: The title expresses the domain as plain “m minus p”, losing the intended manifold-minus-point notation and mathematical typography visible in the statement.
findings.suggested_repair: Set the title’s manifold and puncture notation in supported math delimiters (for example, M\setminus\{p\}).

diagram_candidates.kind: Optional exponential-map domain and boundary-identification schematic
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The source explicitly contrasts injectivity on the open tangent ball of radius pi with the collision of two distinct boundary vectors at the antipode. A paired domain/image picture would make the exact boundary of the normal-coordinate claim easy to verify.
diagram_candidates.content: Draw p on the unit sphere and the antipode -p. Show the open disk B_pi(0_p) in T_pS^n mapped injectively by exp_p onto the sphere with the antipode omitted; show the two boundary points +pi e_1 and -pi e_1 both mapping to -p, with those boundary points excluded from the open disk. Label x_e^i(exp_p(v))=v^i for v in a normal domain D inside the disk. Use an explicitly schematic sphere/disk projection for general n.

diagram_candidates.kind: Optional spherical geodesic triangle / octant diagram
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The source gives an explicit spherical octant, its three vertices, great-circle boundary arcs, right angles, and area; a labeled spherical patch would concretely show the example realizing the angle excess.
diagram_candidates.content: Draw the first-octant patch on S^2_R bounded by the three great-circle arcs between Re_1, Re_2, Re_3. Mark a right-angle interior corner at each vertex, label A=pi R^2/2, and optionally state that its angle sum is 3pi/2=pi+A/R^2. Preserve the outward orientation if arrows are included.

checks.check: The finite stages K_0,K_1,K_2 and C_0,C_1,C_2 show the stated retained intervals: binary halves of lengths 0.4 then 0.16/0.24/0.16/0.16 (with positions matching the source construction), and middle thirds with lengths 1/3 then 1/9. The row labels and shared binary branch labels match the text. It is an illustrative interval-stage picture, not a map-arrow diagram; no orientation, index, or sign defect was seen.

existing_diagram_checks.limitations: All items and assigned tiles in this lane were visually reviewed; the diagram check covers visual consistency with the cited construction, not a general proof audit.

notes: Technique banners are CSS-uppercase styling; that styling is expected. No raw math failure in a technique banner was confirmed in this lane.
Wikilinks intentionally render as block lines. Parenthesis spacing around links is not classified as a rendering defect.
No additional definite raw ASCII formula/title leaks, clipping, or broken LaTeX/TikZ rendering were confirmed in the individually viewed tiles.

The compact-support definition uses display delimiters in source, but the captured HTML renders it as inline KaTeX within the paragraph. The standalone tile shows the expression wrapping and its full tail; classify this as a layout observation, not clipping or omission.

limitations: Every assigned title and ItemBody tile was opened individually at original resolution; per-tile hashes and dimensions are recorded below.
Source, snapshot, HTML, capture metadata, and tile hashes were compared with frozen assignment/capture values; any drift is enumerated in coverage.hash_drift_records.
Diagram candidates are optional and source-supported. No diagram is required as a proof dependency.
